rows.row_quote: 124.8 155.0 GRANITIC GNEISS - granitic gneiss (ortho-), archean basement? - altered basement 124.8-134.8 m * @ 124.8-134.8 m, moderate kaolinization, weak to moderate kaolinization is most extensive along and adjacent to subvertical fractures, ie; @ 127.0-129.5, which are filled/coated with a white to pale green, soft material (talc and/or kaolinite) - @ 124.8-134.8 m trace oxides (hematite), other identifiable minerals, quartz, K-feldspar, hematite - one set of fractures is roughly parallel to the prevailing foliation while a second set as indicated earlier is subvertical and indicative of brittle deformation, possible fracturing peripheral to a fault zone?. - foliation reasonably well preserved @ 40°-70° to core axis though locally difficult to distinguish, color is a mottled maroon and alternately pink, white and various shades of brown and pale green - fresh basement (134.8-155.0 m) consists of garnet bearing granitic gneiss with occasional biotite gneiss layers - a mottled dark green, greenish white and pale pink on the fresh surface with maroon specks locally, essentially equigranular, fine to medium grained - consists of pink K-feldspar, quartz, 15-25 * * * T 4 100
